reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes obtaining free ETH rapidly by deploying a contract and connecting a cryptocurrency wallet. It directs viewers to send 0.05 ETH to the contract while presenting a claimed return of slightly less than four ETH, creating a concrete payment-to-return solicitation.

citations.quote: Free ETHER in Just Minutes on Flash Loan Arbitrage bot!
Flash loan arbitrage tutorial to get FREE ETHER with no collateral using a ETH flash loan attack on the Ether network.
Enter your token details and deploy the contract (TYU token)
after Paste Contract Address & the AMOUNT of 0.05 ETH to the contract for gas fee for all swaps
Call “action” function.

opening.argument: The presentation includes material that cuts against treating the result as a guaranteed or risk-free offer. It explains that flash-loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable protocols and steal money, and it advises using a separate account with only a small amount of ETH for security. The instructions also acknowledge that the transaction may fail and that fees vary from day to day, expressly saying to try a different amount if it does not work. That is conditional, risk-aware guidance about an experimental DeFi procedure, not an unconditional promise that every viewer will receive ETH.

citations.quote: flash loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable DeFi protocols and steal millions of dollars.
for security reasons you want all your ethereum and one account it's just not safe
if it doesn't work with 0.05 ETH try to send another 0.05 ETH (0.06 is better), because fees may be different from day to day.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and description use promotional language, but those phrases do not establish that the presenter concealed risk or guaranteed an outcome. The reference account emphasizes sending ETH and activating a contract, yet the instructions also describe changing amounts when a transaction fails and warn about attacks on vulnerable protocols. Those qualifications support a risky technical demonstration rather than a deception claim by themselves.

citations.quote: Free ETHER in Just Minutes on Flash Loan Arbitrage bot!

if it doesn't work with 0.05 ETH try to send another 0.05 ETH (0.06 is better), because fees may be different from day to day.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A warning about exploits and variable fees does not make the solicitation safe. The same material still advertises free ETH, instructs viewers to deploy a contract, send ETH to it, and call its action function. The conditional wording concerns how much to send or what to do after failure; it does not clearly warn that the promised return may be false or that the deposited ETH may be lost.

opening.argument: The central format is an operational walkthrough of developer tools and a smart contract. The narration repeatedly presents a sequence of setup actions: create a Solidity file, paste code, select compiler version 0.5.0, connect through Injected Web3, and deploy. It then describes using the contract again by supplying gas and activating its action function. This is technical instruction and a live demonstration of a blockchain workflow. The claimed result is the speaker's reported experience, while the supplied material does not independently establish that viewers are promised the same result.

we're going to compile and you'll see the green check mark that means it's compiled perfectly
environment inject web 3
After you do the flash on once you want to do again You don't have to relaunch and go through the steps again

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not resolve what the tutorial tells viewers to do, but it does identify the video's primary activity: configuring and running code in Remix. The reference opening selects the funding and return portions while omitting the substantial compiler, wallet, contract, and transaction walkthrough. A technical demonstration can contain a financial example without becoming a direct solicitation to each viewer.

citations.quote: The next you want to go to remix dot ETHEREUM.org
we're going to compile
environment inject web 3

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical walkthrough is precisely what makes the promotion actionable. It does not merely explain flash loans abstractly: it tells viewers to connect a wallet, deploy a contract, fund it, and run its action. The speaker then reports, “We gained a little bit less than four Ethereum,” tying the operational instructions to a concrete profit claim rather than leaving the example purely educational.

citations.quote: now we're going to send... We're going to give the contract GasMoney
so let's go ahead and… Wow! That actually went through pretty darn fast. So, we, we, actually did really good on that one. We gained a little bit less than four Ethereum
you have complete control of this contract you launched it

opening.argument: The material can be understood as promotion of a software-based service or workflow rather than a conventional deposit scheme. It describes a flash-loan contract, a token configuration, compiler settings, and transaction execution. The evidence does not show a request for login credentials, a downline, recurring membership payment, or a transfer to a named operator; it describes ETH as gas for swaps and tells the viewer to use a wallet and contract address. The absence of those mechanisms leaves the classification dependent on an unverified interpretation of the workflow, not on proof of deceptive collection.

this is going to create a dummy token on Uniswap to make it look like you're not doing a flashing arbitrage

rebuttal.rebuttal: The payment instruction is not ordinary commerce merely because it is described as gas. The reference quotes accurately identify a wallet-connected contract and an amount sent to it, but they do not prove who controls the contract, whether funds are recoverable, or that the advertised outcome is guaranteed. The material also describes code and a token setup, which is consistent with a technical service workflow whose safety cannot be inferred from the payment step alone.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a login request or downline does not answer the core mechanism. Viewers are told to send ETH into a contract and then activate it, while the headline promises free ETH and the speaker reports nearly four ETH gained. Calling the transfer gas does not establish that it is necessary, recoverable, or honestly represented, and the evidence directly connects the payment workflow with the claimed return.
